title: Spinning bridge puck relay and goal
summary: At the start a square puck is sliding along a raised source lane towards the Panda's paddle. Strike it so that it slides onto a platform (the bridge) that spins continuously about a vertical axis, and from the bridge onto an exit lane. Intercept it there with the paddle, strike it again, and send it along the exit lane past a hinged, partly open gate, across a goal line, without the paddle touching it as it crosses and with the gate still open.
robot_setup: One Panda, base at (-0.55, 0, 0) facing +x (yaw 0). Its hand carries a paddle: a flat rigid plate 12 mm thick, 0.10 m wide (2 x `tool_half`) and 50 mm tall, whose face normal is the tool frame's x axis, attached by a fixed adapter bar. The tool frame is the paddle's centre. In the tool frame the hand's TCP is at (-0.12, 0, +0.04). At the start the paddle is upright with identity orientation (faces along world x, width along world y), centre at (-0.08, -0.15, 0.075).
scene: The puck is an orange square block 44 mm x 44 mm x 24 mm thick, quite bouncy. At t = 0 it is sliding towards the paddle on the source lane, a low, very slippery orange slab. If nothing touches it, it slows and stops on the lane shortly before reaching the paddle's start position. Next to the lane's end, a blue rectangular platform (the bridge, 0.20 m x 0.10 m, 20 mm thick) turns continuously about a vertical axis through its centre at a steady slow rate, counterclockwise seen from above. Its top is 2 mm lower than the source lane. Beyond it lies the exit lane, a second slippery orange slab 2 mm lower again. Near the exit lane's far end a hinged gate stands on one side edge: a vertical amber blade 0.12 m long and 55 mm tall with a small knob on its free end. At the start it is swung partly open and still reaches partway across the lane. A very weak spring pulls it towards closed, but the blade's lower edge rests on the lane surface, so it hardly moves unless pushed. Past the end of the exit lane, on the table, is the goal line, with a static orange wall (the backstop, 0.14 m wide, 8 cm tall) behind it. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Puck: box with half extents (0.022, 0.022, 0.012), mass `object_mass` (0.035 kg), friction 0.15, restitution 0.5. At reset it is at (0.06, -0.13 + dy, 0.0465) with velocity (-`incoming_speed`, 0, 0) = -0.35 m/s along x; dy ~ U(-0.012, 0.012) is drawn at reset (first draw). In an idle run it stopped at x of about -0.024 after about 0.4 s, with no paddle contact. Source lane `source_lane`: static slab 0.28 x 0.145 x 0.024 m centred at (-0.08, -0.1175, 0.022), top z = 0.034, spanning x -0.22 to 0.06 and y -0.19 to -0.045, friction 0.025. Bridge `bridge`: revolute fixture with a vertical axis through (0.18, -0.05). The platform 0.20 x 0.10 x 0.02 m is centred on the axis, top at z = 0.032, mass 0.20 kg; at q = 0 its long side is along world x. At reset q0 ~ U(-0.15, 0.15) (second draw), with angular velocity 0.35 rad/s. It is then driven at a constant rate: target q0 + 0.35 t rad, target velocity 0.35 rad/s (PD, kp 80, kd 8, at most 0.5 N m); positive is counterclockwise from above, period of about 17.95 s. Exit lane `exit_lane`: static slab 0.32 x 0.11 x 0.028 m centred at (0.25, 0.12, 0.016), top z = 0.030, spanning x 0.09 to 0.41 and y 0.065 to 0.175, friction 0.04. Gate `gate`: hinge at (0.37, 0.18, 0.03) about world z. The blade is 0.012 x 0.12 x 0.055 m, running from the hinge towards -y at q = 0 (closed: right across the lane), bottom edge at z = 0.03, friction 0.2, restitution 0.35. A knob 0.032 x 0.024 x 0.024 m sits over the blade tip at z = 0.10. Limits [0, 1.3] rad; reset to q = 1.1 rad at rest, with the blade tip at about (0.477, 0.126). Its passive spring drive has target 0, kp 0.00012 N m/rad, kd 0.005 N m s/rad and a cap of 0.25 N m; joint friction 0.00008, damping 0.001. The blade rests on the exit lane's top. In an idle run q stayed at 1.10 for the whole 32 s. Backstop `goal_backstop`: static box 0.02 x 0.14 x 0.08 m centred at (0.54, 0.12, 0.04). Table friction `table_friction` (0.015 in this task). Paddle: `tool_half` 0.05, `tool_mass` 0.2 kg, `tool_friction` 0.3. Horizon `horizon` = 32 s. `goal` = (0.48, 0.12, 0.043) (fixed).

phases.name: physical_bridge_transfer
phases.text: During this phase the puck touches the bridge platform at least once. After that, at some step, the puck touches the exit lane while not touching the bridge.

phases.name: second_strike
phases.text: In this phase the puck first loses contact with the paddle, at time t_s (the first step of the phase without paddle contact; t_s is not reset afterwards). Later the paddle touches the puck again at a time more than 0.035 s after t_s.

phases.name: closing_gate_goal
phases.text: The puck's centre crosses the goal line x = 0.48 (world) moving towards +x between two consecutive physics steps, with its centre within 0.045 m of y = 0.12. At that step the puck does not touch the paddle and the gate's angle is more than 0.20 rad (open). This completes the task. A crossing that fails either check ends the task as a failure.

task_failures: closed_gate_or_carried_puck: in closing_gate_goal, the puck crosses the goal line (as defined there) while touching the paddle or while the gate's angle is 0.20 rad or less.
contact_rules: Only the paddle may touch the puck, and the paddle may touch nothing but the puck: not the lanes, the bridge, the gate, the backstop or the table. No other part of the robot (fingers, hand, links, base) may touch anything.
world_goals_fixed: Goal line: x = 0.48 (world), crossed towards +x with the puck's centre within 0.045 m of y = 0.12. It is announced at reset as `goal_goal` = (0.48, 0.12, 0.043); the z value is not used. Gate angle threshold: more than 0.20 rad at the crossing.
difficulty_note: The transfer depends on the timing of the spinning bridge and on the puck sliding across the 2 mm steps between surfaces. The puck must then be intercepted and struck again on a slippery lane. The final shot has to pass the partly open gate's blade without pushing the gate shut. The episode lasts 32 s.
standard_notes: At t = 0 the puck is already sliding towards the paddle and comes to rest on the source lane within about half a second if untouched. The bridge turns the whole time.
